newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bougainville jumps on PNG govt plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bougainville jumps on PNG govt plan.

text.p: Bougainville Copper Ltd's shares surged five cents or almost nine percent to 61 cents early on Monday after the Papua New Guinea government said on Sunday it wanted to buy RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd's controlling stake in Bougainville's Panguna copper mine.
PNG Prime Minister Julius Chan said the government would approach CRA Ltd with a view to regaining control of the Panguna mine.
Later on Monday, CRA repeated that it had not been formally approached by the PNG government and no talks had been arranged to discuss the offer.
Brokers said the enthusiasm about a possible resolution to Bougainville problem would be restrained until more concrete evidence that the mine might reopen after being shut for eight years.
"Bougainville has had a few runs whenever it looks like there's some sort of resolution," said Burdett, Buckridge and Young dealer Stephen Smith.
"But the overall market will treat it fairly cautiously and wait until there something on the table," Smith said.
"The market will want to see some proof."
Chan said media attention to military training, including the hiring of mercenaries, by Papua New Guinea defence forces had forced the government to announce its plans prematurely.
"The original claims and dispute regarding this mine are at the heart of the Bougainville crisis and (are) critical to a fair and lasting solution," Chan said.
The south Pacific island nation has been fighting seccessionist rebels of the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA) on the island province for the past nine years.
Bougainville closed the Panguna mine in 1989 after a series of sabotage attacks by rebels. Local landowners were disgruntled with the royalty payments being made by the mine's owners.
